purpose: Establish whether the published AE baseline (0.66) is comparable with this project's leak-free protocol.

this_project.protocol: threshold = quantile of the CROSS-FITTED TRAINING score distribution; the scored events never influence it

authors_protocol_read_from_code.threshold_fitted_on: a 20% validation split of the TRAINING data

two_feature_paths_in_package.quick_fault_detection/data_loading.py:ge: keeps every numeric column, INCLUDING status_type_id

authors_protocol_read_from_code.which_path_produced_the_published_score: not recoverable from the code alone

authors_protocol_read_from_paper.source: CARE to Compare, Data 9(12):138 (2024), sec. 4.2.2; arXiv:2404.10320
authors_protocol_read_from_paper.ae_trained_on: 75% of the normal training data, 25% validation
authors_protocol_read_from_paper.threshold_farm_A_and_B: adaptive: an NN predicts the expected reconstruction error, plus a per-farm sensitivity gamma
authors_protocol_read_from_paper.threshold_farm_C: fixed value chosen by maximising the F_1/2 score against ground truth derived from the status-IDs
authors_protocol_read_from_paper.conclusion: the published 0.66 is a TUNED-ON-THE-BENCHMARK number, so it is not directly comparable with a leak-free score
authors_protocol_read_from_paper.feature_scope_difference: the AE sees the full sensor vector (power, wind, pitch, hydraulic, electrical); this project's detector sees only the thermal channels
